entries.author: Dybdal.
entries.note: HK416N (Norwegian Army, 2008) on white, right side: the HK416 receiver, free-float rail, collapsible stock and steel magazine the HK416 F shares; stand-in, the F has ambidextrous A5 controls and a 14.5 in barrel; red dot and vertical grip here are Norwegian fit.

gaps: us_army_ocp: no side profile or straight rear of a standing soldier found; the three-quarter rear and the details cover the carrier back and helmet.
us_army_ocp: no top view (none expected for infantry).
eastern_emr: no side profile or field photo from behind in Ratnik kit; the three-quarter rear is a 2014 parade rehearsal with older helmets and vests on some soldiers.
both: team weapons (machine gun, AT launcher) deployed and carried are not covered in this pass.

german_flecktarn: shared with europe_recon_patrol_light_patrol; no straight rear of a standing soldier; the side view is a 2026 open day, whose coyote carrier differs from the Flecktarn carriers of the other photos (the look takes Flecktarn).

french_cce: Saber Junction 23 (Sept. 2023, 92e RI) photos only; no straight rear; the side view is upper body; helmets are mostly scrimmed or covered, and only one bare F3-type helmet shows its shell (front).

pla_type21: no licensable front or three-quarter front of a PLA soldier in Xingkong woodland with helmet and carrier; the field photos are 2021 Army Games video frames from the side and behind, and whether the uniform is the Type 19 or Type 21 cut is not settled by them; the flat lays give the Type 21 cut and pattern. The helmet in them is a covered high-cut shell, not confirmed as a QGF-11.

hk416f: no licensable clean side photo of the HK416 F itself (Commons' French Army photos are Licence Ouverte, which the library does not allow); an HK416N photo and an HK416 drawing stand in, and the French portrait shows the F-C from the front.
